step_by_step_reasoning: We identify the system's entry point as Kinesis Data Streams (Collect), which ingests real-time security events. The events are loaded into Amazon Neptune (the primary graph database) and propagated to Kinesis Data Streams (Rules) for processing. The graph database replicates data to Elasticsearch (Amazon OpenSearch Service) for indexing/search and DynamoDB for historical tracking. To scale writes, a Shard Service reads CPU and memory metrics from CloudWatch and dynamically balances shard writes. The Rules stream queries Neptune, writes violations to DynamoDB, and alerts users via Email and Slack.

nodes.name: Kinesis Data Streams (Collect)
nodes.notes: Ingests real-time security and compliance configuration event streams from multiple cloud providers.

nodes.name: Neptune
nodes.notes: Highly interconnected graph database storing schema-less cloud resource configurations of over 50M+ resources.

nodes.name: Elasticsearch
nodes.notes: Provides search, slicing and dicing, and aggregation capabilities over resource data.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Acts as secondary backup and stores history of configuration changes as well as detected violations.

nodes.name: CloudWatch
nodes.notes: Monitors CPU, memory, and performance metrics for Neptune and Elasticsearch clusters.

nodes.name: Shard Service
nodes.notes: Intelligent routing service that dynamically load-balances data writes across provisioned Neptune shards.

nodes.name: Kinesis Data Streams (Rules)
nodes.notes: Rules engine data stream that triggers thousands of compliance checks based on incoming resource changes.
